passage:
A digital artwork was sold for a high price online. Students read about it and argued whether digital art could be valuable if anyone could copy the image.
Their teacher compared it to photos of famous paintings. Many people can see copies, but ownership and originality still matter in different ways.
Some students remained doubtful. Others became interested in how technology changes art markets.
The teacher did not force one opinion. She asked students to think about value: Who gives it? What is being bought? Why do people care?
The auction was not only about art. It was about how society decides what is rare in a world of easy copies.
